Subject: E2E p95/p99 latency scoping & benchmark playbook — next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and the immediate asks so we can scope the benchmark and align on pass/fail criteria. I copied Marcus (runtime) and Ben (sales) for any commercial/ops notes.

Summary of Veridian requirements from the call:
- Workload: real-time chat completions powering user-facing replies (single-turn requests).
- Targets (initial ask): p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms end-to-end (client -> app -> Redwood/Incumbent -> model -> client).
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state 2,000 req/min with bursts up to 3,500 req/min; typical concurrency target ~80–120 simultaneous streams.
- Streaming: chunked server-sent tokens (they use an HTTP/2 streaming client), need first-token time guarantees and stable tail-latency.
- Security/comms: all tests must be over TLS, testing keys provided to a test project, no production data.

What Redwood will provide for the benchmark:
- A benchmark playbook (attached: redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.xlsx) detailing test matrix, scripts (locust/jmeter + a custom streaming harness), and measurement definitions (client-observed end-to-end p95/p99 including TLS handshake).
- A short-run smoke test against Hosted API to validate connection/streaming protocol (within 48 hours of keys).
- Full run on Hosted + a comparative run on your incumbent endpoints (we'll compare identical request payloads and concurrency patterns).

Immediate asks from Veridian to scope effort:
1) Can you confirm the traffic shape: 95% small completions (<= 128 tokens), 5% long (>= 512 tokens)? If different, share distribution.
2) Provide sample auth/test key + a sandbox endpoint for the incumbent (or logs if you prefer we drive only against Redwood).
3) Confirm the client streaming behavior (HTTP/1.1 chunked vs HTTP/2) and any proxy/intermediate timeouts.
4) Any geographic constraints (tests should originate from US-east or EU-west)?

Proposed acceptance gates (we can tweak):
- Gate A: p95_end_to_end_hosted <= 200ms for 95% of runs over a 15-minute steady-state window.
- Gate B: p99_end_to_end_hosted <= 600ms and no more than 0.5% of requests > 1s in steady-state.
- Gate C: Superiority or parity vs incumbent: Hosted p95 within 15% of incumbent and p99 no worse than incumbent + 25% (if Redwood shows cost advantages we can relax tail slightly).

Next steps / timeline:
- Today: Alex to share test key and traffic shape (ask 1–2).
- 48h: Redwood smoke test then schedule a 2-hour comparative run (we'll share a calendar invite).
- 1 week: Full benchmark report + raw CSV results + suggested runtime tuning (batching/quantization routing).

If that looks right I'll open the benchmark ticket and schedule dates.

Thanks,
Priya

Thanks Alex / Priya — a few engineering clarifications from my side so the measurement apples-to-apples: 

1) Measurement path: we will capture client-observed end-to-end (complete request to first token + stream completion) and also split out server processing time (time in runtime) and network/TCP/TLS handshake time. Please confirm if Veridian wants TLS handshake included — many customers exclude it but your requirement earlier suggested inclusive.

2) Streaming first-byte vs token cadence: we'll report both first-byte latency (time to first token) and median token inter-arrival for steady-state. For p99 we recommend measuring tail over 5-minute sliding windows and reporting 95th/99th percentiles of first-byte and complete-response times.

3) Concurrency model for the test harness: Redwood will run tests at target concurrency of 100 streams with spikes to 250 streams for 60s to simulate bursts. We'll align on the exact spike timing with Alex.

4) Warm caches: We will run a 10-minute warmup to populate KV caches and quantization paths; first-run artifacts will be excluded from acceptance windows.

I'll prepare a short test-run checklist and add it to the playbook. Priya — once Alex shares the sandbox key I'll spin up the smoke test and share the exact JMeter/locust command-lines.

-Marcus
